text:
Samir: Hey team, Samir here  joining today! Quicks: 1) I'm neurodivergent and sometimes struggle with time-limited training modules. Is there an accommodation path for the mandatory security modules / phishing sim? 2) I primarily use Linux (Fedora) for dev work  does the MDM/endpoint policy cover Linux or should I request a company Mac?
Maya (People Ops): Welcome Samir :tada: Great qs. For accommodations we can extend deadlines or provide alternative formats. Please DM me or reply here and well route to People Ops + Security. For devices, our MDM primarily supports macOS and iOS; Linux machines are allowed but need an approved enrollment flow. Tagging @Ellen (Security) for details.
Ellen (Security): Hi @Samir  thanks for surfacing this. Accommodations: we can mark your training as "extended window" and exclude you from the live phishing cohort during the first 30 days if you prefer. To set it up we need a short note from people-ops consenting to the extension.
Samir: That would be perfect  I get anxious with timed quizzes. Appreciate it.
Ellen (Security): Noted. @Maya can you confirm the accommodation entry and we'll update the training system. Also re: Linux: we support minimal agent enrollment for Linux (OS-level policies + VPN cert) but some device management features (MDM profiles, FileVault) are macOS-only. If you keep secrets off-device and use the company laptop for privileged work, Linux is fine.
Samir: Helpful. So what do I need to install on Fedora to get basic compliance?
IT Desk: Hi Samir  IT Desk here. For Linux devs we require: 1) company VPN client (OpenConnect) + cert, 2) disk encryption (LUKS recommended), 3) OS updates enabled, 4) an approved endpoint agent we call "rdw-agent" (lightweight) for inventory and compliance checks. We'll send a setup doc.
Samir: Any commands for LUKS status? I'm comfortable with CLI.
Ellen (Security): To check if root is encrypted, on many distros run: ```lsblk -f``` and confirm the root partition has crypt type. For Fedora with LUKS: ```cryptsetup status <name>``` should show active. If unsure, open an IT ticket and we can assist.
Samir: Cool. About phishing sims  can you share examples so I know what to look for? I worry about clicking something by accident.
security-bot: Automated message: Phishing simulations are labeled in the subject with "[Redwood Simulation]" and originate from simulation@redwood-security.test. Report simulated emails using the report button and you'll receive a brief micro-training email instead of a penalty. More at https://intranet.redwood.com/security/phishing-sims
Ellen (Security): Also: we never ask for full credentials in an email. If an email asks you to enter creds on a form, hover over links (don't click) and verify domain. For any doubt, use the report button or DM security. We can temporarily opt you out for the first 30 days per the accommodation.
Samir: Thank you all  please mark me for the extended window. I'll DM @Maya with the note. One more small ask: will enrolling Linux agent expose my personal files?
IT Desk: The rdw-agent only reports installed packages, kernel version, and compliance flags. It does not upload personal files. We only request metadata needed for security posture.
Maya (People Ops): Confirmed  I filed the accommodation note: "extended training window 30d for Samir". @Ellen please update the training system when you can.
Ellen (Security): Done  training window extended and initial phishing cohort opt-out set. Samir, you'll get an email confirming the change and a friendly reminder after 2 weeks.
Samir: Amazing, appreciate the quick help :heart: I'll DM the form and start the Linux setup.
Maya (People Ops): Welcome again :wave: shout if anything blocks you, we can set up a screen share for the Linux agent install.
